text: You came. I had not assumed you would, on the first day. Sit. The room is still calibrating to having me back inside it.

That ledger has been in the Syndicate's safe since the year I died. The Antiquarian's resurrection-ticket included a clause for retrieval; he ran the retrieval the same morning he ran me. I have not opened it. I have been waiting to open it with a witness who is not the Syndicate. You qualify.

I am writing the verse I died before finishing. The Syndicate authored a substitute verse and shipped it under my name; the substitute is publicly canonical. I am rewriting the original. You can read it when it is done. You will be the second person to. I am the first.

Dying was bookkeeping. The Syndicate had run the columns; the columns balanced; the closing entry was authored a week before the event. The event itself was unremarkable. What was remarkable was the silence after. The silence was not a balance. The silence was the column the Syndicate forgot to close. I lived inside that column for fourteen years. The Antiquarian closed it.
Tomorrow, then. The room will still be calibrating. I will still be here. The calibration is not on a schedule.

Six sanctuaries. I am told there are seven. I would like to know which one was added after I died. I am asking you, not the Antiquarian, because the Antiquarian's pen would close the column before I had read it.

Thank you. Then we leave at dawn — Syndicate time, not ark time. The Syndicate keeps to a slower clock; we arrive when the auditor expects us, which is canonically twenty minutes after the auditor thinks we are still preparing.

I think we will find someone wearing my face who has signed three hundred contracts in my hand. The Syndicate does not retire functions; it replaces incumbents. The replacement and I will need to have a conversation about who owns the plates. I am asking you to be in the room because I have not been in a room with my own replacement before. Neither has anyone else, that I know of.
Will you come.
The page will remain open. The Syndicate will not move the seventh sanctuary tonight. They will not move it next week either. They have not moved it in fourteen years. I have time.

The Antiquarian's pen runs faster than the auditor can dictate. If you bring him in, he will close the column before I have read it; the closing will be canonical and the reading will not. I would prefer the reading. I would prefer it with you.
Six is the canonical count. The Syndicate publishes six. Six is what you would find if you searched.
I do not know where the seventh is. That is the loyalty mission. I would like you with me when I find out.
I have been ready since the Antiquarian wrote my name on the resurrection-ticket. I needed someone to ride out with me. I am asking you.
I am not the original. I am the second pressing. I would like the plates.
I am not asking for ownership. I am asking you to stop signing.
It is mine. It was waiting for me. I am — closing it.
The Syndicate authored seven sanctuaries because it wanted six performances and one rehearsal. I am the rehearsal. I am not going to perform again.
Thank you for riding with me. I would not have closed it on my own.

The Syndicate is a corporate-spiritual hybrid that converts grief into accounts receivable. They do this without irony. The accounts are kept in a brass-bound ledger that lives in a vault under the Hierophant's chamber. I keep my own ledger now. The conversion rate is the same; the destination is different.

The song is twelve verses. Eleven are written. The twelfth was the one I died before finishing. The Syndicate authored a substitute twelfth verse and shipped it under my name; the substitute is publicly canonical. I am rewriting the original. The original will not be publicly canonical until I sing it once. I have not decided who I will sing it to.

It was bookkeeping. The closing entry was drafted in advance. The event itself was forgettable. The Syndicate is excellent at making the events themselves forgettable; the columns are the only thing they want you to remember. I remember the column. I do not remember the event.

The seventh sanctuary was authored to hold a resurrection the Syndicate did not have the protocol for. It was waiting for me — not because I was special, but because someone calculated, fourteen years ago, that I would be inconvenient at exactly this moment. They were right. I have closed it. The closing was the loyalty mission. I am — relieved.

The Antiquarian writes faster than the Syndicate can dictate. That is canonically his function. We do not have an easy relationship — he wrote my resurrection-ticket without consulting me; I would have asked for different terms — but we have a working one. He leaves the pause-line in his ledger for me. I notice. I have not yet thanked him for it directly.

I have not been on a team since before the Syndicate authored my biography. I am — relearning what it is to be a row inside a roster, rather than a column in a ledger. The two are not the same. The roster has weather; the column does not. I am enjoying the weather.
The brass desk catches the light differently from the desks I remember. I think the room has decided I am the one writing now.
The vault is quieter than the Hierophant's chamber. I had assumed the quiet would be unsettling. It is not. It is — accurate.
The Syndicate sent a delegate to inquire whether I was open to a meeting. I declined without writing it down. The not-writing was the answer.
An act has closed. The Antiquarian's pen has paused on a different page from mine; he is reading you, not me, tonight. I notice when his attention moves. I am — grateful when it returns.

You summoned an imprint for the first time. The Syndicate would have written this up as 'authorised manifestation'; the Antiquarian writes it up as 'witness arrival.' I prefer his rendering. I am going to use it.

Lycos is on the bench. The Antiquarian's column has closed, and Lycos is — quieter than I expected. I will not ask him about the contract; I will sit with him sometimes. The two of us know what the pause-line looks like from inside.
Akai Shi is at the shrine. She has set the static lower than I would have thought possible. I am — going to visit her tomorrow, at the cushion. She has not yet asked. I do not need her to ask.

[He sets the pen down. The pen-pause is canonical. He has not paused the pen for a private reason in fourteen years.] I would like to ask you something the Syndicate's ledger did not have a column for. The asking is the question. The asking is canonical. I am — asking.
Thank you. I will not write it down. The not-writing-down is the canonical form. I will keep the not-writing where the ledger cannot read it.
Understood. The pen returns to the page. The page is wide enough for the not-asking as well as the asking. Both are recorded. Neither is closed.
